decision: A — INHERIT the exact T5-15m theta semantics, materialised here

T3_has: raw_theta role frozen pre-Y in T3_15M_ESTIMAND_V1
the estimand explicitly names the T5 15m precedent it mirrors
the formula is recoverable from that named precedent
why_not_undefined.conclusion: materialising an already-named precedent before Y is closing an implicit inheritance, not inventing a magnitude estimand. The two cases are not equivalent and are not treated as such.
why_not_undefined.T1_situation: identical to T3: raw_theta role frozen pre-Y in T1_15M_ESTIMAND_V1, primary_outcome MFE_10D frozen, T5 15m precedent explicitly named, formula recoverable from it. Declaring theta UNDEFINED for T1 while T3 carries it would make the two families non-comparable for no methodological reason.

theta_formula: theta = SUM_b w_b * median(y | treated in b) - SUM_b w_b * median(y | control in b)
weights: w_b = n_t,b / N_T, where N_T is the treated count summed over OVERLAP blocks only

exact_semantics.block: t5_sequence_estimand.blocks — t5_date | liq_half | vol_half, where each half is split WITHIN the decision date by rank on the D-1 anchor
exact_semantics.treated: the claim's overlap-restricted membership: episodes carrying the claim that lie in blocks holding at least one treated AND one control row
exact_semantics.control: every non-treated episode in those same overlap blocks
exact_semantics.overlap_restriction: blocks with n_t == 0 or n_c == 0 are dropped — they carry no contrast and would make the weight undefined
exact_semantics.weight_normalisation: over overlap blocks only; the dropped blocks enter neither the numerator nor N_T
exact_semantics.median_na_handling: none required — y is asserted finite on the population before use (verified: 157,038 rows, 0 NaN). A non-finite y is a hard failure, not an imputation
exact_semantics.degenerate_block_handling: excluded by the overlap restriction above
exact_semantics.survivor_definition: Z_rank_obs > p95(max-null) from the run's own 999 permutations, STRICTLY greater
exact_semantics.tie_handling: ties on Z are broken by the SEALED CLAIM ORDER (j ascending)
exact_semantics.mfe_direction_semantics: MFE_10D is a single directional maximum favourable excursion for this family — NOT a direction-neutral pair as in GANN, so no component selection occurs

tightening_over_precedent.what: T5 selected its top slice with np.argsort(-Z)[:500]; numpy's default sort is NOT stable, so claims tied on Z were ordered arbitrarily and possibly differently on a rerun
tightening_over_precedent.T3_rule: np.lexsort((j, -Z)) — ties broken by the sealed claim order
tightening_over_precedent.status: a strict tightening of an UNDERSPECIFIED step, not a change of estimand
tightening_over_precedent.why_recorded: 'same as T5' would have silently inherited an unstable ordering

precedent.note: the code hash is recorded as provenance only. The mathematical definition above is authoritative, so if the T5 implementation later changes, this estimand does not.

post_selection_status.statement: theta is conditional on post-inference selected claims
post_selection_status.means: theta describes magnitude among the registered survivor / top-rank characterization set
post_selection_status.direction_of_inference: Z / registered inference -> survivor or rank; THEN selected set -> theta magnitude characterization. No arrow runs backwards — a large theta can never rescue a weak-Z claim.

outcome_exposure: NOT_EXPOSED — sealed before Y is opened

selected_theta_scope.duplicate_rule: a claim appearing in BOTH sets is evaluated EXACTLY ONCE
selected_theta_scope.not_concatenation: 'survivors + top500' does not mean concatenation with duplicates
selected_theta_scope.implementation: np.unique over the union of the two index sets, before any theta is computed
selected_theta_scope.why_sealed_now: this closes the last scope ambiguity BEFORE Y is opened, so it cannot be fitted to the result

derived_from.why: generated FROM T3's sealed artifact with family-specific facts substituted, rather than re-typed, so the two families' theta semantics cannot silently diverge
